newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds static up to US CPI, Swedish budget.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds static up to US CPI, Swedish budget.

text.p: Danish bond prices were near-static on Tuesday in a thin market, cautious ahead of the afternoon's U.S. March CPI data and the Swedish budget.
"We are treading water up to the American data and the Swedish budget announcement. Turnover has been thin and fluctuations minimal," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.02 point up from the pre-market at 108.96, 0.14 point up on Monday's close, yielding 6.63 percent in turnover of 1.2 billion crowns. The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two basis points to 72.
The 2006 benchmark's June future was 0.13 point up at 108.42 in 23 volume. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 fell 0.07 point to 87.23.
The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8080 per mark at 1115 gmt.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling 230 million crowns worth of mainly the seven percent 2007 state bond as part of its routine financing operations.
